title: Workflow run steps rely on bash defaults for fail-fast; do not add set -euo pipefail
answers: should run step use set -e in copilot-agent workflow
why no set -euo pipefail in workflow bash script
does a failed gh api call fail the GitHub Actions step
body:
Convention: .github/workflows/copilot-agent.yml sets defaults.run.shell to bash. GitHub Actions runs that shell with --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail.
Consequence: a failed `gh api` command substitution or a failing `jq` pipeline already fails the step, so an explicit `set -euo pipefail` in run: blocks is redundant here.
Constraints: This holds only while defaults.run.shell stays bash. If a step overrides shell (e.g. sh or a custom shell template), add explicit error handling there.
applies: Run steps in .github/workflows/copilot-agent.yml that inherit the workflow default shell.
says: Make sure our automated assistant workflow halts immediately when an API request fails.
The bot automation step kept running even though a command within it failed.
Ensure automated helper steps terminate right away when any pipeline command encounters an error.
search: In .github/workflows/copilot-agent.yml, run steps inherit defaults.run.shell set to bash, which GitHub Actions automatically runs with --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail. Because failed gh api command substitutions or failing jq pipelines already fail the step, explicit set -euo pipefail commands in run blocks are redundant. This fail-fast behavior only applies while using the default bash shell; steps that override shell, such as sh or custom templates, require explicit error handling.
